title: SDK Buffered Acceptance Project-Local Split Review
purpose: Review orchestrator/run-buffered-acceptance.mjs for any safe reusable SDK core boundary while preserving AE Agent governance, documentation, package-script, and evidence-policy checks.

rationale: The runner's durable value is the AE Agent local governance contract: M152+ packet validators, direct current smoke checks, README assertions, package script assertions, and exact evidence paths.
The only neutral candidates are small forced-read-only defaults and argument rejection mechanics, but extracting them would add an interface without reducing current complexity or validation risk.
The buffered SDK acceptance path still owns live SDKThread creation for acceptance reports; this milestone does not have approval to run or refactor SDKThread/network behavior.
Keeping the file project-local avoids diluting fail-closed governance checks while the reusable write-runner core has already been separated in M160-M169.

keepProjectLocalReasons: The collectors hard-code AE Agent audit directories for scope review, readiness, approval-decision, enablement, and launch-governance packets.
The validation expectations intentionally know M152 production-code provider smoke governance and the disabled CEP-panel lane.
Moving them to neutral core would require an adapter plugin interface but would not reduce the current runner's active risk.
The contract smoke directly calls current M152+ governance, conveyor, extraction, archive, and provider-lane smoke scripts.
Those checks are AE Agent continuity evidence rather than reusable SDK orchestration semantics.
Retiring or moving any of them would be cleanup work, not a behavior-preserving neutral extraction.
The assertions pin this repository's package command names and entrypoints.
They guard AE Agent review and handoff workflow expectations.
A standalone tool should be called by these scripts, not own these repository-specific script names.
The README checks intentionally assert exact AE Agent milestone snippets and audit artifact names.
They preserve documentation/governance parity for this project.
A generic README checker would either be too weak or need the same project-specific data injected back in.
The evidence policy is tied to this repository's milestone chain, forbidden work boundaries, and reviewable commit cadence.
The active governance report must keep reading the committed AE Agent M152 packets.
The handoff and plan updates are project continuity artifacts, not reusable SDK core.

neutralBoundaryAssessment.reason: The contract is tiny, already source-visible, and coupled to the acceptance wrapper's local SDKThread prompt/report path; extraction would add churn without meaningful reuse today.

reusableResponsibilities: reject flag values for boolean modes
neutralBoundaryAssessment.reason: The parser is small and exported already; a neutral parser would still need the AE Agent unsafe-flag set and command modes injected.
The actual checks are dominated by AE Agent package, README, governance, and artifact assertions; a generic shell would leave the hard parts project-local.

preservedContracts: codex:orchestrator:governance-report still points to node orchestrator/run-buffered-acceptance.mjs --governance-report
check:rules still points to node orchestrator/run-buffered-acceptance.mjs --contract-smoke
governance report output remains sdk-launch-governance-drift-report.v1 from the M152 launch governance packet and M152 production-code enablement packet
buffered acceptance unsafe overrides remain rejected before SDK thread creation
validationPlan: configured local smoke suite from AGENTS.md
